interpretation: This measures seven JS compiler variants, not additional Rust speedup.

Linux/Windows combined paired P50 savings versus same-loader control are 19.23–26.02% on retail and 18.76–20.37% on Wevu across their four OS/batch observations. Their pressure savings are 1.45–5.56%; these ranges do not include macOS.

macOS combined paired P50 savings are -1.154% / 4.709% on pressure, 19.486% / 18.407% on retail and 20.909% / -2.054% on Wevu in batches 1 / 2. macOS Wevu batch 2 is a counterexample to uniform real-page gains.

Paired savings quantiles summarize per-pair ratios, not a ratio of separately computed wall quantiles. macOS Wevu batch 2 control/optimized wall P50 values are 25.23425 / 19.097125 ms (24.321% lower), while paired savings P50 is -2.054%; 21 of its 42 pairs improve and 21 regress. Keep both statistics without substituting one for the other.

Combined wall P95 improves versus control in all twelve Linux/Windows groups and four of six macOS groups. macOS pressure batch 2 and Wevu batch 2 wall P95 increase 3.161% and 10.899%; Wevu values are 36.479459 / 40.45525 ms. Shared-runner variability does not justify discarding these counterexamples.
Linux props-no-scope Wevu batch 2 wall P95 is 8.21% worse; Windows pressure batch 2 ast-reuse and props-no-scope wall P95 are 7.45% and 14.12% worse.

macOS retail batch 2 ast-reuse, page-meta-gate and reserved-props-gate wall P95 increase 13.911%, 11.179% and 21.695%; Wevu batch 2 ast-reuse, props-no-scope, page-meta-gate and reserved-props-gate increase 24.106%, 25.361%, 47.966% and 7.958%. Single-feature results must remain visible.

Baseline/control loader effects exist: Linux pressure/retail wall P95 increases 5.64–7.03%; Windows loader RSS P50 increases 4.35–19.72%. macOS Wevu baseline/control wall P95 changes by +17.104% / -20.077% in batches 1 / 2. Use the same-loader control, and do not promise production memory savings or dismiss regressions as loader noise.

macOS combined pressure batch 1 RSS P50 increases 2.513%; other macOS combined RSS P50 values decrease. Pressure batch 1 props-no-scope, page-meta-gate and reserved-props-gate RSS P50 increase 5.427%, 6.062% and 5.937%. These are worker snapshots, not production memory acceptance.

Each platform independently verifies 230 source hashes, 14 report hashes (one correctness summary, seven correctness workers and six timing reports), 448 correctness checks, 42 initial timing checks and 1764 timed observations; 396 quantiles and 1512 per-pair records are recomputed per platform, totalling 1188 quantiles and 4536 pairs. The top-level summary digest is additionally retained in rawManifest.
Reserved-props gate does not skip work on pressure; apparent single-feature gains there cannot be attributed to eliminating analysis.
No cross-corpus/batch pooling, no summing independent feature percentages, no adding these gains to prior Rust experiment percentages.
Warm compileVueFile with diagnostic hooks and fixed options; not cold builds, Vite/HMR, runtime or the production 10%/5% gate.
RSS is post-compile worker snapshot, not peak or process-tree memory. CPU includes all process threads; Windows CPU accounting is coarse.
macOS uses Node 24.20.0/arm64/3 CPUs; Linux and Windows use Node 24.21.0/x64/4 CPUs. Absolute timings across platforms are not directly comparable.
Shared runner contention is not independently measured. The two batches are repeated observations, not a statistical significance claim.
Per-round positions and within-round predecessor pairs are balanced; boundaries between rounds are not uniformly balanced.
Raw warmup observations are not persisted; 14 warmup rounds are recorded and enforced by the source protocol, not independently recounted from artifacts.
Correctness worker artifacts contain full serialized outputs; timed reports only retain output digests after in-process full comparisons.
Source identity covers the declared 230 files and real corpus blobs, not every installed dependency file.
